Colleagues and students, I have a brief but important announcement regarding the scanning electron microscope. Over the past month, we've seen a sharp increase in requests, and the current booking system—essentially first come, first served—has led to a few groups reserving large blocks of time they ultimately don't use. Effective next Monday, we're introducing two changes. First, no single user may book more than six hours per week in advance; additional time can be claimed only within forty-eight hours of an open slot. Second, if you fail to show up for a booking without canceling at least twelve hours ahead, your advance booking privileges will be suspended for two weeks. These measures aren't intended to penalize anyone, but rather to ensure that graduate students with thesis deadlines aren't crowded out.
question: What problem led to the new booking rules?
choices: The microscope has been breaking down frequently.
Too few people have been using the microscope.
Some users reserved time that went unused.
Graduate students have been damaging samples.
answer: Some users reserved time that went unused.
explanation: 一部のグループが大量に予約し、実際には使わないことがあったため。
